pieces.label: She stands in a hospital gown with a gold halo behind her blonde bob and holds up a scan of her own spine like a holy image. Small flames burn among the leaves; an armadillo and a monkey keep watch. In *The Broken Column*, Kahlo painted her spine as cracked stone. This one has been scanned, and the halo is not a joke. It is a claim about who gets to be the saint.

pieces.title: Self-Portrait on the Bus
pieces.subject: a woman with short black curls and hoop earrings seated on a city bus staring out at the viewer, an invented person who resembles no real painter, other passengers as small folk-art figures, a parrot on the seat back
pieces.label: She sits on the bus in a red dress with black curls and gold hoops, a woven bag on her lap, and looks at us as if we were the ones who should not be here. Behind her the other passengers are small and simple, and the jungle presses at the windows. A parrot sits on the seat back. Kahlo's *The Bus* is full of strangers too. It did not have a parrot.

artists.name: Andy Warhol
artists.wallText: Warhol screenprinted soup cans and film stars until fame and groceries looked the same. He predicted that everyone would be famous for fifteen minutes. He undershot. He would be delighted.
artists.styleBrief: Pop art silkscreen on canvas, a photographic image reduced to high-contrast flat blocks of garish colour, repeated in a grid with slight misregistration between prints, acid pink, yellow, turquoise and black, deadpan commercial flatness, screen texture and ink bleed
artists.subjectRule: Modern mass objects and modern fame, repeated until they mean nothing and everything.
artists.renderSuffix: museum photograph of the silkscreen canvases, flat even lighting, no frame, no text, no wall, no floor, cropped to the canvas edge

pieces.title: Thirty-Two Energy Drinks
pieces.subject: a grid of thirty-two identical unlabelled tall slim aluminium cans in flat garish colours, slight misregistration
pieces.label: Rows of tall slim cans in pink, yellow and turquoise, with no names on them, each printed slightly off its own outline. The title says thirty-two. Count them: there are twenty-four. The other eight have been drunk. Warhol printed thirty-two soup cans, one for each flavour, and said he had eaten the same lunch every day for twenty years. The cans have changed. The lunch has not.

pieces.title: Wireless Earbuds Diptych
pieces.subject: a pair of white wireless earbuds in their open case repeated in a four by four grid, each in a different acid colour combination
pieces.label: Sixteen open cases of white earbuds in a four-by-four grid, each on its own acid ground: yellow, pink, turquoise, black. The misregistration makes the white buds shiver. Warhol loved an object that everybody owned, because the president drinks the same Coke as the man on the corner. Everybody owns these too. Hardly anybody still owns both of them after a year.

pieces.title: Ring Light, Nine Times
pieces.subject: a stylised young face with a ring-light reflection in each eye, repeated nine times in flat pink, yellow and turquoise with black screen halftone
pieces.label: The same young face nine times over, in pink, yellow and turquoise, with black halftone for the shadows and a small ring light caught in each eye. Warhol made his *Marilyns* from a single publicity still and repeated it until the woman disappeared into the picture. This face was already a picture when it was taken. Nine is modest. The original was posted four hundred times.

pieces.title: Cardboard Boxes
pieces.subject: a stack of plain brown cardboard delivery boxes printed in flat brown and black with one box in electric pink
pieces.label: Stacks of brown cardboard boxes, printed in flat brown and black, repeated nine times across a grid of yellow, turquoise and pink. In the middle one stack has gone electric pink, the way one parcel in a hundred arrives in the wrong colour. Warhol stacked printed Brillo boxes on a gallery floor as if they were sculpture. These are already stacked in every hallway in the city.

pieces.title: Cable
pieces.subject: a single white charging cable coiled on a bright yellow ground, printed with crude black screen outline, repeated twice side by side
pieces.label: A white charging cable, coiled, plug at one end and connector at the other, printed four times over on yellow, pink and turquoise with the crude black outline of a cheap screen. It is the most important object in the house and it is always in another room. Warhol would have printed it in gold and sold it for a fortune. He would have lost it by Tuesday.

artists.name: Yayoi Kusama
artists.wallText: Kusama has covered pumpkins, rooms, people and the walls of the world in dots since the 1950s. Her infinity rooms have hour-long queues. Here the dots cover the things we queue for.
artists.styleBrief: Contemporary painting of obsessive repeated dots and nets, dense polka dots in graduated sizes covering every surface, red on white, yellow on black, undulating net patterns, hallucinatory flatness, the object dissolving into pattern, thick even acrylic with hand-painted irregularity
artists.subjectRule: Modern objects consumed by dots until the object almost disappears.
artists.renderSuffix: museum photograph of the acrylic painting, flat even lighting, no frame, no text, no wall, no floor, cropped to the canvas edge

pieces.title: Scooter
pieces.subject: an electric kick scooter covered entirely in black dots on yellow against a yellow ground of larger dots, almost dissolving
pieces.label: An electric scooter stands on a yellow ground covered in black dots, and it is covered in black dots itself, so that it only just holds its shape. The dots on the floor are big and the dots on the wall small, which is the only way you know where one ends. Kusama has dotted pumpkins for most of her life. The scooter is the pumpkin of the pavement: everywhere, and faintly absurd.

pieces.title: Phone, Obliterated
pieces.subject: a smartphone lying on a table where phone, table and shadow are all covered in red dots on white, the phone barely distinguishable
pieces.label: A phone lies on a table, and the phone, the table, its shadow and the wall behind are all covered in red dots on white, so that the phone is only a slightly raised rectangle in the pattern. It has vanished into its surroundings, which is the opposite of what a phone usually does. Kusama speaks of self-obliteration, letting the dots erase the self. This is phone obliteration. It is very restful.

pieces.title: Sneakers
pieces.subject: a pair of chunky white sneakers covered in graduated red dots on a red dotted ground
pieces.label: A pair of chunky white trainers, covered in red dots that shrink as they climb towards the laces, standing on a floor and against a wall covered in bigger red dots. The shoes have nearly disappeared and are still, somehow, very expensive. Kusama has dotted handbags, shoes and whole shopfronts in her time. She knows exactly how much a dot adds to the price. She is not telling.

pieces.title: Server Rack with Net
pieces.subject: a tall server rack dissolving into an all-over white net pattern on pale grey, tiny blinking dots of green
pieces.label: A tall black server rack, its rows of green lights blinking, stands in a corner that two patterns are taking over: red dots on the left, a pale grey net on the right. The net is already creeping on to the rack. Kusama painted her infinity nets loop by loop for hours without stopping, as a way of holding on. The server does the same, without stopping, for everyone.

pieces.title: The Queue
pieces.subject: a long queue of simplified figures covered in black and yellow dots, all facing the same direction, the queue curving into a dotted infinity
pieces.label: Black silhouettes covered in yellow dots stand in single file, all facing the same way, and the queue curves up and away into a dotted figure of eight: the sign for infinity. The ground under them is pink with red dots. The queues outside Kusama's infinity rooms last for hours. This is the queue with the room taken away. Nobody in it has noticed the difference.

artists.name: David Hockney
artists.wallText: Hockney has never stopped changing tools: swimming pools in acrylic, Polaroid joiners, faxes, iPad drawings. Sunlight has been his subject for sixty years. He is the one painter here who is already doing this. This wing is a tribute.
artists.styleBrief: Contemporary painting in flat bright acrylic, clean Californian sunlight, saturated turquoise, pink, lime and yellow, simplified forms with crisp edges, patterned water and foliage, a calm sense of leisure and space, flat colour with occasional wobbly hand-drawn line, slight digital-drawing smoothness
artists.subjectRule: Sunlit modern leisure and modern landscape, painted with obvious pleasure.
artists.renderSuffix: museum photograph of the acrylic painting, bright even lighting, no frame, no text, no wall, no floor, cropped to the canvas edge

pieces.title: Cannonball, Filmed
pieces.subject: a turquoise backyard pool, a huge white splash from a cannonball, a phone on a tripod filming it, a pink house and one palm
pieces.label: A turquoise pool, a pink house, one palm, and in the middle a huge white splash where someone has just gone in. Nobody is visible: the diver is under water. The only witness is a phone on a tripod in the foreground, filming. Hockney said *A Bigger Splash* took two weeks to paint and the real thing lasts two seconds. The phone gets it in one.

pieces.title: Electric Car, Canyon Road
pieces.subject: a small white electric car on a winding road through stylised hills in lime, orange and violet under a flat blue sky
pieces.label: A small white electric car takes the bends of a coast road between lime hills, an orange slope and a violet ridge, with a blue sea below and an agave in the corner. You can tell it makes no noise. Hockney painted the winding roads of the Hollywood hills as a map you could drive with your eye. The car is quiet enough to hear the colours.

pieces.title: Portrait of a Friend on a Tablet
pieces.subject: a man in a striped shirt seated in a bright room drawing on a tablet, a bowl of lemons, a blue chair
pieces.label: A man in a striped shirt sits by the open terrace door with a tablet on his knee, drawing the view, while a bowl of lemons and an empty blue chair keep him company. The sea shines outside. Hockney began drawing on a phone around 2009, then on a tablet, and has not stopped since. This is a portrait of a friend doing what Hockney does, in his light.

pieces.title: House with Solar Roof
pieces.subject: a modernist house with a dark blue solar roof against a pink evening sky, a lawn in flat green, a sprinkler arc
pieces.label: A low modernist house under a pink evening sky, its roof laid with dark blue solar panels, a flat green lawn in front and a sprinkler throwing a dotted arc of water across it. Palm trees, and a sun like a coin. Hockney painted Los Angeles lawns and sprinklers in the sixties as the height of luxury. The luxury has moved up to the roof. The sprinkler has not noticed.

pieces.title: Hawthorn in Blossom, Filmed
pieces.subject: a hedgerow bursting into blossom in flat bright greens and whites, a small figure filming it with a phone, a tractor far off
pieces.label: A hedge of hawthorn bursts white along a slope in spring, and a woman in a straw hat stands in front of it filming it on her phone. Far off, a tiny red tractor crosses a yellow field above the estuary. Hockney has spent years recording the arrival of spring, day by day, first in Yorkshire and then in Normandy. She is doing the same. He would tell her to look for longer.

artists.name: Jean-Michel Basquiat
artists.wallText: Basquiat painted like someone taking notes on the whole world at once: anatomy, jazz, prices, crowns, words crossed out so you would read them harder. Today's world takes more notes than ever. Few of them are this alive.
artists.styleBrief: Neo-expressionist painting in acrylic and oilstick, raw urgent figures with skull-like heads and exposed anatomy, scrawled crossed-out words and symbols, three-pointed crowns, arrows and lists, layered colour fields of yellow, red, blue and black on raw canvas, drips and smears, wooden stretcher bars visible at the edges
artists.subjectRule: Modern anatomy of systems: apps, prices, hustle, algorithms. Words are allowed only as scrawled paint.
artists.renderSuffix: museum photograph of the painting on rough canvas, flat even lighting, no frame, no wall, no floor, cropped to the canvas edge

pieces.title: Untitled (Gig)
pieces.subject: a raw skull-headed figure on a bicycle with a delivery bag, crossed-out scrawled price tags and arrows around it, a three-pointed crown above, yellow and black
pieces.label: A skeleton on a bicycle, a delivery box on its back with a crown drawn on the lid, rides through a storm of crossed-out prices: $12.99, $9.99, $6.50, $4.99. A list at the left runs food, money, time, life. The words at the right say faster, cheaper, better, happier. Basquiat crowned the people the city looked past. This rider gets several crowns and no tip.

pieces.title: Anatomy of a Hand Holding a Phone
pieces.subject: a diagram-like painting of a hand and forearm with bones and tendons labelled in scrawled marks, gripping a rectangle, red and blue on cream
pieces.label: An arm stretches across the canvas, skinless, labelled like a textbook: radius, ulna, tendons, metacarpals, phalanges, and at the end of it the hand grips a phone. Around it, lists: grip, hold, take, keep; survive, create, destroy, repeat. Basquiat learned his anatomy from the copy of *Gray's Anatomy* his mother gave him in hospital when he was seven. This is what the hand is for now.

pieces.title: Untitled (Per Month)
pieces.subject: a large painting of a crowned figure surrounded by a repeated scrawled list of crossed-out numbers and small symbols, dripping black on yellow
pieces.label: A crowned skeleton stands in the middle, flanked by two columns of numbers, one to forty, each struck through as if another month had gone. The words say king, power, money, freedom, glory, death, and at the bottom: past, present, future, none. Basquiat crossed words out, he said, so that you would want to read them more. You will read every one of these numbers on your statement.

pieces.title: Untitled (Server)
pieces.subject: a grid of black rectangles with scrawled white marks, a small crowned figure in the corner, red arrows pointing in every direction
pieces.label: Nine black rectangles in a grid, each scratched with white marks, crowns and scribbles, and red arrows shooting out of them in every direction, like data, or blood. A skeletal figure stands at the left with its heart showing. In the bottom right corner one tiny crowned figure sits, head in hands. Near it: no more lies. Basquiat filed the world in grids of notes. This grid files him back.

pieces.title: Self-Portrait with Earbuds
pieces.subject: a raw frontal self-portrait of a young Black man with a shaved head and white earbuds, an invented person who resembles no real painter, crown above, layered blue and yellow fields, scratched marks
pieces.label: A young man with a shaved head looks straight out through layers of blue and yellow, white earbuds in, a crown above him and a skeleton on either side. The writing around him says still here, bigger than the pain and, with a question mark, a better tomorrow. Basquiat painted himself crowned, haloed and furious. This one is quieter. The earbuds are doing some of the work.
